title: How a hole in the ground becomes a swimming pool

beats.text: If you dig a hole in your backyard and fill it with water, you have a pool. But dirt drinks water, so it needs a concrete shell.
Under the lawn: topsoil, clay, sand, and groundwater.
But concrete on wet dirt cracks, so the floor gets a bed of gravel to drain it.
And rising groundwater can push an empty pool right out of the ground. So the floor gets a valve that lets it in. This is a relief valve.
But still water turns green, so pipes run from a drain and a skimmer to a pump.
But concrete cracks when it's pulled, so a steel grid goes in first, and concrete is fired onto it from a hose. This is shotcrete.
Then you keep it wet for days, because concrete doesn't dry, it cures.
But raw concrete scrapes skin, so it gets smooth plaster, tiles and a stone edge.
Now fill it: twenty thousand litres, about twenty tons of water.
A pump pushes it through a sand filter and back, the whole pool every six hours.
Add a ladder and some sun. Congratulations, you've built a pool.
